newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Gold slides to lowest fix in three years.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gold slides to lowest fix in three years.

text.p: Gold prices slipped to their lowest level since November 3, 1993 on the first afternoon of trading of the year and some bullion dealers saw further losses to come.
Bullion fixed at $366.55 per ounce on Thursday afternoon after $367.80 that morning, itself a four week low. On Tuesday, before the New Year holiday, it was set at $369.55.
Dealers said that the largely United States-based investment funds still anticipated weaker gold price and that any further falls would play into the fund managers' hands.
"Technically the market looks awful and it did not start the year well at all. The funds will be happy to put a bit of pressure on to bring prices down further," a senior dealer said.
Another dealer noted that almost all the gold activity was coming on the floor of New York's Comex futures market.
"We saw some fund selling on Comex just before the fixing. Before that there really wasn't any direction in the market after the holidays," one dealer said.
The February Comex futures contract ended down $2.00 at $369.20 on Tuesday, with most of the pressure coming in the closing minutes of the session.

"It is very inconsistent just now. The Dow (Dow-Jones industrial average) was off about 100 points on Tuesday yet gold still fell. With loose money sloshing around you would have though it would have gone somewhere like gold," a dealer said.
The Dow was lower again on Thursday afternoon as gold prices slipped about $1.50 from their earlier levels to a low of $366.00.
"I think we can expect to see that being threatened later," a London-based dealer forecast.
The outlook was still largely negative. "A gold clear-out would be good for gold. I can see it down to $330-$340 in the early part of this year," a dealer said.

However, market analysts responding to a recent Reuters' poll widely forecast a price correction on the soaring U.S. stock markets helping to lift gold prices from the trough in which they closed out 1996 as investment funds switched some cash from equities to bullion.
Rhona O'Connell at stockbroker T. Hoare and Co said, "A stockmarket meltdown could change everything."

But a more direct threat to the gold market in 1997 was expected to come from the central banks, especially in Europe, which were re-assess their largely dormant and non-revenue earning gold reserves, several analyst said.
"Producer selling and central bank selling in response to a price rally will stop gold and silver going above their historic highs (in 1997)," one analyst said.
Early in 1996, gold prices soared to their highest levels since before the Gulf War as the investment funds piled into the market.
Gold bull run topped out at over $416.00 on February 2, its highest price since February 22, 1990, but the rally was short lived.
By the end of June, bullion was valued at around $380.00, a low not seen since September 1995 and a slower but inexorable diminution in value has continued every since.
